... and doubling the cube: https://github.com/wwylele/Compass

I gave a shot at theorem number 8 from Freek Wiedijk's list of 100 theorems, and this is what I got. I think the main difficulty comes from stating the theorem. So my first question is, does the definition and the statement look correct? (The Challenge.lean file contains the extracted definition and theorem)

If this looks correct, should I add this repo to the 100.yml file, assuming there isn't another candidate pending?

And finally, how much of this is in the scope of upstreaming to the Mathlib? I don't mean upstreaming the code in its current messy state. I want to know whether the following definitions should go into Mathlib after cleaning up

  • Constructible numbers
  • Constrictible points/lines/circles
  • The theorem itself (in Archive?)

A thing I often do in compass-straightedge constructions is to choose an arbitrary point from within an open set, and make use of the point for some intermediate constructions, as long as the final result doesn't depend on the specific choice of point I used. Your definition excludes such constructions, does that sound like something you might wanna include?

I thought about it, but I found it hard to formalize. One way I can think of to formalize statements (without changing the my definition of constructibility) would be

theorem something_is_constructible_with_an_arbitrary_point
(s : Set P) (hs : IsOpen s) (ha : a \mem s): ConstructiblePoint {a, ...} ... := ...

theorem something_is_not_constructible_with_any_number_of_arbitrary_point
[Fintype ι] (f : ι → Set P) (hf : ∀ i, IsOpen (f s))  :
¬ ∃ ..., ConstructiblePoint {points in f, ...} ....  :=..

I haven't thought deep on how to actually prove second kind of statement

On the other hand, I somewhat convinced myself that any construction that asks for choosing an arbitrary point should work the same if it is required to choose from the initial point set, so the ability of arbitrary choice shouldn't allow much more.

For reference, the constructibility rule was taken from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straightedge_and_compass_construction#The_basic_constructions, which doesn't mention allowing picking a random point

Here is an argument why choosing an arbitrary point doesn't need to be explicitly added to the constructibility rule (though it relies on theorems yet to be proved in the repo): when there are at least two starting points, the set of all constructible points is dense. If the instruction says "pick a point from open set S", one can repeately draw a lot of constructive points until one lands in the set S. This also applies to some non-open set like "picking a point on the line": find two constructible points in the neightborhood of the line, draw another line and find the intersection

I'd hope mathlib would end up with enough material on geometrical constructions to be able to use it to (a) prove such theorems about what is constructible, (b) exhibit explicit constructions for e.g. a regular 17-gon and (c) state and solve six early IMO problems asking for some kind of geometrical construction (1959 P4, 1959 P6 (in three dimensions), 1960 P4, 1961 P5, 1962 P5, 1967 P4; note: I don't know enough of the history of mathematical pedagogy in eastern Europe in the 1950s and 1960s to be sure exactly what would have been considered a legitimate construction in that context for those problems).

I am working towards (a) and getting pretty close. My current definition of constructibility, which is a Prop with proof irrelevance, doesn't require constructive instruction of how to draw everything. The difficulty of constructive instructions comes from things like "choose a point among two intersections" (arbitrary choice, or choice conditioned on geometric relationship) or "if this happens to be a degenerate case, do something else" (decidability on real)

Update: I have the converse theorem (constructible numer -> constructible point) at EuclideanGeometry.constructiblePoint_of_mem_constructibleClosure. This can be used for proving what is constructible

I have the theorem that characterize constructible polygon at EuclideanGeometry.constructible_polygon. Of course, as previously mentioned, it doesn't contain the explicit construction due to ConstructiblePoint being a Prop.
btw I previously opened #41757 to link 100.yml to my repo. Thought I should mention it here
